problem: End-to-end image-goal navigation must implicitly learn many subtasks at once, and modular approaches rely on metric maps. Both are computationally heavy, slow to update, generalize poorly, and are hard to deploy on resource-constrained devices.
motivation: Navigating to a specific location or instance given an image in unknown environments is critical for real robots, which often have limited compute (e.g., no CUDA). The paper is driven by the idea that topological, reachability-based knowledge plus object co-occurrence priors can replace metric maps and cut computation.
key_idea: Dual Graph Navigation combines an External Knowledge Graph of object correlations, built from small datasets, with an Internal Knowledge Graph of explored objects linked by reachability. The IKG dynamically updates the EKG to guide instance-image navigation in a plug-and-play modular pipeline.
insight: Replacing metric maps with topological, reachability-based graphs lowers computation, which yields a reported 3.8 to 5.5 times faster decision-making than baselines and lets the system run on edge devices without CUDA. Modular components that can be trained independently and swapped are claimed to improve generalization across AI2-THOR and Habitat. Only the abstract is available, so no ablation evidence can be cited.
method: External Knowledge Graph (EKG): built from small-scale datasets to capture prior object correlations and guide target exploration.
Internal Knowledge Graph (IKG): built online with an instance-aware module, recording explored objects by reachability relationships instead of precise metric information.
EKG-IKG dynamic update: the IKG updates the EKG so priors adapt to the current environment, giving topological perception.
Plug-and-play modular design: functional modules are trained independently and can be replaced flexibly, reducing training and deployment cost.

setting.backbone: Modular pipeline with independently trained lightweight modules (instance-aware module plus knowledge-graph-based exploration); specific models not stated in the abstract
setting.training_data: Small-scale datasets used to build the EKG and train modules; details not given in the abstract
setting.observation: egocentric RGB image observations with a goal image (details not stated in the abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only; no numeric results available (abstract only states SOTA on ProcTHOR-10K and 3.8-5.5x faster decisions)
results: The abstract reports state-of-the-art performance on the ProcTHOR-10K dataset and good generalization across AI2-THOR and Habitat. It also reports deployment on three real robot platforms, including edge devices without CUDA, and decision-making 3.8 to 5.5 times faster than baselines. No numeric metrics are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so metrics, baselines and ablations could not be verified.
Reliance on object-correlation priors from small datasets may limit performance in environments with unusual layouts.
